newsitem.title: USA: SEC seeks Miami finance info from Fla firms - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: SEC seeks Miami finance info from Fla firms - lawyer.

text.p: "Virtually every bond house in Florida" has received an informal request for information from the Securities and Exchange Commission in relation to City of Miami finances, an attorney for a government witness said Thursday.

The attorney, Richard Burton, represents bond underwriting firm Howard Gary & Co. Its chairman, Howard Gary, is cooperating with the U.S. Attorney's Office in its probe of public finance corruption in Miami and Dade County.

Burton made the comments at a meeting among attorneys working on upcoming bond issues for the Dade County Housing Finance Authority. The attorneys were wrangling about what, if anything, should be disclosed in bond documents about Gary's involvement in the probe.
Gary's firm is one of two financial advisers for an upcoming $8 million multifamily housing bond issue by the authority.
Burton questioned where the disclosure line should be drawn, noting that many firms that have been involved in Miami bond issues had received the SEC requests for information.
"Will everyone who's received one of these letter have to write a disclosure?" Burton said. "That's virtually every bond house in Florida."

City officials have previously disclosed that the SEC was investigating the city's bond issues, but underwriters contacted by Reuters have declined to say whether they had been questioned or asked for information.
"There is no indication what anyone is being asked and why," Burton told Reuters after the housing authority attorneys' meeting.

The attorneys agreed that a sentence describing Gary's involvement in the U.S. Attorney's probe should be included in the bond offering statements, and hoped to draft exact language by the end of the week.

Attorneys for Gary and his firm previously disclosed that Gary was cooperating with investigators in the probe, which already resulted in indictments against former City Manager Cesar Odio, city lobbyist Jorge Luis de Cardenas and former City Commissioner Miller Dawkins.
Dawkins has pleaded guilty to conspiracy charges and admitted he accepted $75,000 in kickbacks from a company seeking a computer contract with the city.
The city is also wrestling with a $68 million budget deficit that has raised eyebrows among municipal securities regulators.

At Thursday's meeting, Gary gave housing athority lawyers copies of a brief letter from Assistant U.S. Attorney Mary Butler stating that "Howard Gary & Co is not now a subject or a target of the grand jury's investigation into political corruption in Miami or Metro-Dade County known as Operation Greenpalm." The letter was dated Oct 30.

The attorneys for the housing deal said they were uncertain whether Gary's involvement in the probe was material, since the issues were guaranteed by Fannie Mae, and since Gary's firm was one of two financial advisers on the deal. Raymond James & Associates Inc is the other.
"There are others out there who have looked at the transaction and feel it makes sense," said Janet O'Brien, bond counsel for the $8 million issue.
Still, said Dade County Attorney Gerald Heffernan, "I think it's important to put the potential bond holders on notice about all this."
